grep resolves a symlinked search root to its real path
revert and fork select messages by ID comparison instead of position

runs.output:
I'll start by reading the TrieRouter implementation.`src/router/trie-router/node.ts:203` — non-global regex in the multi-part-param resume calculation.

```
m[0].match(/\//)?.length   →   m[0].match(/\//g)?.length
```

`String.match` with a non-global regex returns `[match]` — length always `1`. So `componentCount` (parts consumed by a multi-part regexp capture) was clamped to `0` or `1` regardless of how many `/` the capture actually spanned.

- Symptom 1: capture spanning ≥3 parts (`foo/bar/baz`) requeued the child node at `curNodesQueue[1]` instead of `[2]` → resumed mid-capture, `file.html` never matched → 404. Depths 1–2 worked by coincidence (0 and 1 slashes are correct under both).
- Symptom 2: `/:file{.*}/*` on `/a/b/c` — capture consumes all 3 parts, so the node should never resume. Under-counting resurrected it at the final part, where the `'*'` pattern branch pushed the same handler already pushed by the full-match `child.#children['*']` branch → duplicate.

Both reproductions now correct; full suite 4744 passed. Pre-existing `tsc` errors in `client.test.ts` / `jsx/*.test.tsx` are unrelated and untouched.

I'll find the grep tool implementation.`packages/opencode/src/tool/grep.ts:60` — root cause: `FSUtil.resolve(requested)` ran `realpathSync`, so the search root (and therefore `cwd`, and therefore every `path.resolve(cwd, item.entry.path)` result row) was rewritten to the symlink target. Replaced with `path.resolve(FSUtil.windowsPath(requested))` — still absolutizes and applies Windows drive-form normalization, but no longer collapses symlinks.

Consequences fixed together: reported match paths now stay under the caller's path, and since the external-directory glob is derived from the same unresolved `requested`, an allow rule on the alias directory matches the paths actually touched.

Verified: `bun test test/tool/grep.test.ts` 6 pass, `bun run typecheck` clean. `FSUtil.resolve` in `edit.ts:38` left alone — realpath is correct there (lock identity must be per inode).

I'll start by locating the revert and fork logic.Root cause: cut points were chosen by lexicographic ID comparison over the (correctly ordered) message list. Fixed by locating the target message positionally in that list.

- `session/session.ts:709` — fork prefix now `msgs.slice(0, indexOf(messageID))` instead of `break` on `msg.info.id >= input.messageID`. Unknown/absent messageID → full copy, as before.
- `session/revert.ts:75` — diff range now `all.slice(indexOf(rev.messageID))` instead of `filter(id >= rev.messageID)`.
- `session/revert.ts:110` — cleanup removes everything from the target index onward (target itself kept only when `partID` is set) instead of comparing `id <`/`id >`.

Typecheck passes. Left `message-v2.ts:591` (`latest()`) alone — out of scope for revert/fork, though it shares the same ID-ordering assumption.
